scope: Every tracked tests/**/*.sh and tests/**/*.ps1, including helpers, executable fixture simulators and golden wrappers. This reviews the test harness boundary, not a substitute for reviewing the production code it tests.
method: Enumerate complete tracked population, enumerate eight risky sink families, review source/caller/consumer contexts for dynamic source, native argv, serialized fixture data, regex paths, protocol types/case, process status and cleanup. Inspect generated-program and wrapper dependencies separately. Candidate matches and syntax checks are indexing aids, not independent semantic proofs.

contexts.launchers: Fixed interpreter programs and quoted/array argv delegate to a named Python/Node verifier. exec or LASTEXITCODE propagates failure; interpreter lookup is a capability check. A launcher is not independent semantic coverage of its delegate.
contexts.golden: Capture uses a pinned Git revision and disposable snapshot; promotion validates manifest identity, source hashes, exact target inventory and content hashes before replacement. The CI and human-identifier guards precede writes. Graders delegate to golden-eval.py. These are frozen baselines and evaluation tools, not product runtime branches.
contexts.fixture-infrastructure: Fixture builders own fresh temporary trees; finite enum arguments define shape, loop drivers use jq/argv and check subprocess status before advancing. Lite simulator is explicitly synthetic; object/array/type and exact-token controls were repaired. Comment-only registry wrapper siblings intentionally contain no implementation.
contexts.installer: Install/uninstall tests use fake native CLIs and separate temporary roots; observable filesystem manifests, command receipts and exact status are the oracle. Generated shell paths now use a shell literal; PS process arguments use the existing native encoder. Bracket-root controls preserve a neighboring tree across rollback/upgrade/removal. Config paths use serialization. Installed product behavior is tested through actual installer entry points.
contexts.host-and-guard: Adversarial command strings and malformed envelopes are input data to guards, not commands executed by the harness. Native guard wrappers capture status/JSON; empty stdin is malformed input and is now checked as actual exit2. Live handoff is separately opt-in and source/config checks do not claim live-host evidence. Synthetic denial fixtures remain labeled synthetic.
contexts.model-collection: Panelist/model fixtures emit bounded fixed test verdicts and deliberately malformed bodies, with finite task/model/digest values. Arbitrary scratch paths cross argv or escaped fixture literals. Timeout/signal tests own children and completion receipts. Production timeout algorithms are reviewed by their owner; test code is not a replacement implementation.
contexts.workflow-review: Workflow/review fixtures mutate isolated feature trees or restore saved live registry state in finally/trap. Root relocation now uses literal byte replacement, preserving document bytes apart from the intended path. Hashes are derived from actual fixture files. Negative tests deliberately construct bad provenance/approval/contract documents; those strings are inputs to the validator.
contexts.canonicalization-approval: Raw-byte capture avoids PowerShell text-redirection normalization where byte identity is asserted. Signing/weakening helpers call literal Python with paths as argv, including independent HMAC recomputation. Hash/key fixtures are synthetic; fixed expected hashes are test vectors, not policy copies. Error-category assertions supplement actual nonzero status.
contexts.capability-ownership: Registry/resolver/ownership tests use explicit fixture schemas, process result objects and diagnostics; schema identifiers and lowercase digest grammar are exact when asserted. Positive/negative and mutation fixtures exercise general validators. Case-insensitive prose checks are documentation assertions rather than acceptance of protocol tokens.
contexts.lite: Lite tests distinguish actual CLI chains from the explicitly named step-2 simulator. The simulator now rejects malformed root/member shapes and wrong-case tokens; its presence does not demonstrate an agent executed a skill. Baseline frozen helpers are retained as compatibility references, not current production validators.
contexts.domain: Pester suites invoke both actual domain validator twins and use native process capture for byte-level comparisons. The v2 child-v1 suite is a fixed generated program with suite path supplied as argv. Literal invalid JSON/domain strings are intentional negative corpus; runtime result counts and statuses remain asserted. Case grammar oracle tightened.
contexts.design: Design scanner/compliance tests use source and runtime fixtures with explicit paths and expected state. Embedded DSL/YAML/JSON snippets are either closed fixtures or serialized values. Design-sync command failure semantics and current compliance scalar tests have a separate owner handoff; their concurrent deltas must retain their own source hashes.
contexts.documentation-release: Document/template and release wiring tests inspect fixed source artifacts using literal checks or authored regex. Numeric heading range selection now uses literal prefixes. Extracted workflow command bodies are trusted repository code executed with test doubles, not untrusted data concatenation. Source presence checks are not represented as execution of a live release.
contexts.other-contracts: Integration/compatibility/encoding contracts use finite fixture matrices, isolated paths, explicit expected status and output assertions. Raw text/byte oracles are kept distinct from semantic JSON comparisons. Existing direct runtime invocations retain their language-specific argument boundaries.
contexts.publication: Human-copy tests distinguish candidate staging from actual publish and rollback; fixed protected manifests and byte receipts are independent inputs. Native streams are captured as bytes, target paths use literal operations, and failure-injection cases intentionally corrupt only disposable copies. Native phase-2 Windows contracts are source reviewed here and require their Windows execution lane.
contexts.byte-runtime: Compatibility, CRLF, path and constant-parity matrices compare bytes or named semantic fields across actual runtimes. Expected artifacts are explicit fixtures; no implicit conversion of raw bytes into text for byte-identity claims. Fixture mutation injectors alter disposable copies and must change the expected outcome.
contexts.runner-selfcheck: Catalog, deterministic-lane and coding adapter tests inspect/run the declared verification boundary. The PowerShell adapter is separately reviewed by checker owner: native AST diagnostics and a narrow machine subset do not establish all semantic rules. Skip allowance requires manifest identities and fingerprints; SKIP text is not a successful runtime execution.
contexts.gate-integration: Cross-script gate/scenario regressions use direct commands or fresh native hosts, explicit counters and fixture mutations. The suite is an acceptance consumer of the production scripts, not another runtime implementation. Runtime-oracle case was tightened where protocol identifiers/digests were read; diagnostic prose matching can remain case-insensitive.
